transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-19
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Dr. Sofia Ramos (CalyxHealth ML Lead), Ethan Chen (CalyxHealth CTO), Priya Nair (CalyxHealth PM)

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. quick intro — I'm Maya, AE on this account, and Jordan is our solutions engineer. do you want to do quick intros on your side?
[00:12] Sofia Ramos: yeah hi i'm Sofia, ML lead at CalyxHealth. we run NLP workflows for clinical summarization and patient triage, mostly english and spanish.
[00:22] Ethan Chen: Ethan here, CTO — i'll be focused on infra and security constraints.
[00:28] Priya Nair: Priya, product manager, i'm driving timeline and success metrics.
[00:33] Jordan Lee: great, thanks. the goal for today is scoping the POC: success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks and picking an open-model shortlist that balances quality/cost and multilingual support.
[00:45] Maya Patel: quick note — we're assuming a two-week benchmark window and want to propose both hosted and dedicated options depending on your security needs. are you leaning private/VPC or hosted for the POC?
[00:58] Ethan Chen: security first — ideally VPC peering with customer-managed keys. SOC2 is required; we may need air-gapped later but for POC VPC + KMS should be ok.
[01:12] Jordan Lee: that's fine, we can run Redwood Private in your VPC for the benchmark. we'll include KMS integration and audit logs in the POC scope.
[01:22] Priya Nair: timeline-wise, we want to validate quality metrics and throughput within three weeks max — two weeks for benchmarking and a week to review and decision.
[01:34] Maya Patel: sounds reasonable. let's pin success criteria — Sofia? what are the must-haves for model output?
[01:42] Sofia Ramos: top things: clinical accuracy for summaries (low hallucination), consistency across english/spanish, latency under ~300ms for single-turn summarization, and maintain PHI safety — must never output patient-identifiable data. We also want F1-style metrics for named entity extraction and a human review sampling pass rate above 95% for critical fields.
[02:05] Jordan Lee: good, we'll include hallucination rate checks and sampling. For PHI safety, we can add sanitization in the pipeline and run red-teaming prompts during the benchmark.
[02:17] Maya Patel: workload sizing — can you share average prompt/context lengths and QPS?
[02:22] Priya Nair: typical prompt length is ~120 tokens, average returned summary ~400 tokens, peak concurrent requests around 15 QPS during business hours, but most of the day is 2-4 QPS. monthly volume for POC scale is small but projected to 10M tokens/month if we go prod.
[02:39] Jordan Lee: ok so for benchmark we'll simulate spikes to 20 QPS and target tail latency SLOs. we'll call out batching strategies and KV caching options.
[02:50] Maya Patel: model shortlist — we recommend testing 3-4 open models that match your requirements. Jordan, do you want to walk through options?
[02:56] Jordan Lee: sure. candidates: 1) Llama 2 70B (fine-tuned variant) — strong general capabilities, good multilingual baseline but needs careful safety fine-tuning; 2) Mistral Large or Mistral 7B Instruct — good cost/quality tradeoff, fast; 3) Falcon 40B — strong for English and lower hallucination on some biomedical prompts in our internal tests; 4) RedPajama / Mosaic-based 34B variants — cheaper but may need more instruction tuning for clinical tasks. we can also include a distilled quantized run (8-bit/4-bit) to compare latency/cost.
[03:45] Sofia Ramos: for Spanish support, we've seen Llama variants do okay, but domain-specific Spanish (medical terms) is hit or miss. do you have multilingual bench results?
[03:56] Jordan Lee: we do; we'll include Spanish prompt sets in the benchmark. for strict clinical Spanish, we may recommend fine-tuning on your corpus. as part of POC we can measure zero-shot vs fine-tune uplift.
[04:10] Ethan Chen: cost question — how different is hosted vs dedicated for these models? pricing ballpark would help.
[04:17] Maya Patel: ballpark: hosted per-token costs vary by model size and qps; dedicated (reserved capacity) gives predictable throughput and lower per-token for sustained load. we'll include both options in the proposal. for example, quantized Falcon/distilled models can reduce per-token by 30-50%.
[04:34] Priya Nair: what about latency — do bigger models always mean worse latency?
[04:38] Jordan Lee: generally larger models increase per-token latency, but kernel optimizations, batching, and KV cache impact this. Redwood runtime can prioritize low-latency routing and fallback to smaller variants if tail latency spikes. we'll configure autoscale/burst for your POC.
[04:55] Maya Patel: any regulatory/data residency concerns?
[04:57] Ethan Chen: for now US region only, but must have audit logs, retention policies, and KMS. also need contract language about data never being used to further train public models.
[05:09] Jordan Lee: we have enterprise controls for that; will include legal/security packet.
[05:14] Sofia Ramos: benchmarks — we want: 1) accuracy metrics (NER F1, summary ROUGE/clinically-oriented metrics), 2) hallucination rate measured via red-team prompts and reference checks, 3) latency percentiles p50/p95/p99 under synthetic traffic, 4) cost per 1k tokens. Also compare zero-shot vs 1-3 epoch fine-tune on 1k examples.
[05:38] Jordan Lee: got it. for the bench plan, we'll run each model across your sample set, run multilingual subsets, and simulate bursts. we'll capture p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec for each config (quantized and FP16).
[05:52] Priya Nair: can you also show a simple evaluation harness? Our team wants to reproduce results locally.
[05:58] Jordan Lee: we'll hand over the benchmark harness (pytest-like scripts + load generator) and a results spreadsheet.
[06:05] Maya Patel: any blockers on dataset sharing? Sofia?
[06:09] Sofia Ramos: we'll anonymize PHI for POC but provide representative examples and schema. expect about 500 records for the initial run.
[06:16] Ethan Chen: and we'll confirm networking — VPC peering and KMS details — by Friday.
[06:22] Jordan Lee: for the model shortlist, do you want us to include a commercial closed model baseline (e.g., OpenAI) for quality comparison?
[06:29] Priya Nair: yes include a closed baseline if possible, helps justify tradeoffs.
[06:34] Sofia Ramos: also include any pre-existing benchmarks you have in the healthcare domain.
[06:38] Jordan Lee: we'll include Redwood's internal med-bench snapshots and a red-teaming set.
[06:43] Maya Patel: tradeoffs — we'll present quality vs latency vs cost charts, and we'll recommend default: start with Falcon 40B quantized for english-heavy flows, and Mistral/Llama fine-tuned for bilingual flows depending on uplift.
[06:57] Sofia Ramos: fine — a practical question: what does the POC cloud footprint look like? GPUs, memory?
[07:04] Jordan Lee: for Falcon 40B quantized you can run on 2x A100/80GB or equivalent with optimized kernels; Mistral/Llama smaller variants can run on 1x A40 or T4 for quantized runs. we'll include exact machine types in the benchmark spec.
[07:19] Ethan Chen: if we have to run on-prem, can Redwood support an air-gapped installer?
[07:23] Jordan Lee: yes, Redwood Private has an on-prem package; for POC VPC-peered deployment is easiest, air-gapped needs additional lead time. we'll note that in timeline.
[07:33] Priya Nair: Ok let's recap timeline and deliverables.
[07:36] Maya Patel: recap: Redwood to send POC proposal + pricing by 2026-04-21; Jordan to send benchmark plan + hardware spec by 2026-04-22; customer to share anonymized sample data and success metric definitions by 2026-04-22; schedule benchmark week of 2026-04-26; run two-week benchmark and review on/around 2026-05-10.
[07:58] Sofia Ramos: that works. any quick blockers?
[08:01] Ethan Chen: confirm SOC2 docs and data handling language in contract — key blocker for us to approve dedicated or on-prem later.
[08:12] Maya Patel: will include SOC2 and legal clauses.
[08:15] Priya Nair: last question — can you test a small fine-tune (1000 examples) during POC or is that out of scope?
[08:22] Jordan Lee: we can include a small fine-tune experiment on a forked model for uplift measurements; will need compute and dataset, but doable in the two-week window as a controlled experiment.
[08:33] Sofia Ramos: ok great. thanks everyone.
[08:36] Maya Patel: thanks — we'll send the proposal and benchmark docs and follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark window.
[08:44] End of recording.

Notes on transcription: occasional filler words removed for readability; some proper nouns (model names) may be transcribed slightly off in the raw export. Links referenced: POC proposal (to be sent), security packet (link to enterprise security doc), Redwood internal med-bench (internal link).
